utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can -- I'll just pause, Your Honour, because of the noise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness BU, in order to move as efficiently this morning as possible, I want to direct your attention, please, straight away to the bundle of documents that have been put before you. And if you can find in that bundle of documents what is marked as 09713. It should be the first document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you turn to the document itself, I see you're looking at a cover page at the moment, but if you look at the actual document behind that tab -- you're not on the correct document, sir. If you can find 9713, it should be the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, that's not the right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, you forgot to give us a brief summary of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just one moment. Let me sort out one thing at a time here. For some reason - my apology, Your Honour - there is not a tab. It is the first document in the bundle, but for some reason there is not a tab. Your Honour, this witness will testify to events in Prozor municipality. His full statement covers a period from 1992 into the latter -- to the middle part, or so, of 1993, starting with events in that municipality, with particular focus on events in the village of Toscanica. I don't want to say any more than that based upon the protective measures in terms of the particular village. He will concentrate in particular on events around that area, in particular during the period April 1993, concerning an attack on that village and the expulsion of Muslims from that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you should have before you -- my apology, there was no -- there was no tab to that particular item. But if you have now before you P 09713, you will see there that if you see -- if you look at the document, you will see first that there is an English version and then behind that there is a Bosnian version. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you gave an interview to an investigator from the ICTY on the 2nd of October, 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, but I can't remember. I know I gave an interview in Mostar. I remember that, but I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's possible. I won't say that's not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At that time, sir, a written statement was prepared in the English language and interpreted to you in your own language. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't read out to me. It wasn't necessary, since the interpreter interpreted and it was typed out immediately. It wasn't necessary for me to read it out. I had faith in the person who had transcribed what was said. There were certain changes, perhaps, or certain things were perhaps taken out of context or it wasn't written correctly. For example, it says, "up until the liberation of Jablanica," it should have said "up until the liberation of Toscanica" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One step at a time. Listen to my question, please. One step at a time. I'll ask you if there are any corrections that you've wanted to make, or that you want to make today. Directing your attention -- in the English version, if you look to the last page of the English version of the document -- it might not be on the last page. But you'll see there -- on the bottom of the first page, did you put your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And on each of the pages, if you leaf through the English version, did you put your initials on each page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct. That's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, since coming to The Hague a day or two ago, were you provided a Bosnian language version of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you read and review that statement? And again, I'm specifically referring now to the Bosnian version of your statement, since coming to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I ahead it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I'm not asking you now what the corrections are. My question is simply: Are there any corrections that you would like to make to your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there are corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you now --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: For the assistance of everyone in the courtroom, Your Honour, since this statement was not prepared with paragraph numbers, I've circulated a version of the material which is identical in content, except that paragraph numbers have been assigned for ease of reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, you will see there in front of you, it should be in your bundle, a copy of your statement both in English and B/C/S that has numbers written on the side of the paragraphs. Do you have that? All right. Let me direct your attention, please, first of all, to paragraph number 4, if you can find that. In that paragraph, sir, is the correction you wish to make that you actually completed school -- your school in the village or hamlet called Hudutsko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention, please, to paragraph number 17. In that paragraph there was use of the word, and reference in the first sentence there was reference to the word or phrase, "heavy artillery." And you wish to change that to "mortars."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were two mortars. There was no heavy artillery. Heavy artillery is a very broad concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me next direct your attention, please, to paragraph 35. Do you wish to correct, sir, that it was not Nijaz Gagula who went into the village with you on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he stayed there. You can see -- well, he was with me but he remained with another group because we had split up. He set off in one direction and we headed off in the direction of Toscanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Other than Mr. Gagula, did two other men actually accompany you into the village itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Mirsad Vila and Dzevad Piralic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can next ask you to look at paragraph 40. I believe this is the one -- the correction you were about to say a few minutes ago. Actually, this was an error in the -- not in the English statement but in the translation that was then provided. Was there a misuse of the reference to the liberation of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think there's a similar error. I was in Toscanica last time, but the mistake was when it says Jablanica was liberated instead of Toscanica. But we'll get to that mistake, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, but the correct reference in terms of the liberation, the location was Toscanica and not Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The last time I was in Toscanica, not in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. And then finally can I ask you, please, to look at paragraph 41. And at the end of the next-to-last sentence of that paragraph are the words -- it ends with the words "all of them were executed by a gun-fire." Do you wish to correct that by saying "all were killed in Toscanica"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were all killed in Toscanica. When an exhumation was performed, they asked me how many dead there were in Toscanica and I said five. I didn't mention any names. But later there was some confusion and it seemed that everyone had been killed by gun-fire. One of them hadn't even been killed when these people were killed. That's the woman whom we'll deal with later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. And, sir, taking those corrections, then, in mind - and there will be some other items that you will expand upon in the further parts of your testimony today when we get to those particular parts - but with those corrections in mind, sir, with this statement, then, if I were to take you today through all the matters in your statement, does this statement, which has been marked as Exhibit P 09713, would this be your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the same questions and 3.000 others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Now, sir, I'm going to go very quickly through the first part of your statement, and, as I've explained to you before, the Judges have your entire statement. It's not that other parts of your statement are not important, but because of time and because the Judges have your entire statement, I will focus -- I want to direct your attention to particular items so we can hopefully finish your testimony today. I do want to direct your attention, please, to paragraph number 9 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, I'm not sure I agree with that kind of procedure. You confirmed the entirety of his written declaration through the witness, so there's no need to draw our attention to the different parts of it. We'll read it, and I think that the best thing would be for you to go on to the documents. There are a lot of documents, so why not ask him about the documents rather than have him re-state what he's already said in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There are certain points of clarification. The way we've handled the 92 ter witnesses so far, many of them, there are certain points of clarification or further explanation that the witness can give or corrections that -- additions that he's made. And that's -- I'm going to ask him about those specific items without, in fact, going through the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Counsel Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I don't agree with what Mr. Scott has said. Corrections are one thing; additions are another. And that is quite contrary to your guidelines. If we look at the transcript of the 25th of September, page 7159 we can't add things to the statement. That is why I object to having new elements added in the course of this procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this results from the proofing sessions, and he made five corrections during that time. Now I think you should go into discussing the documents. So I disagree with the method of asking direct questions again. So either you're going to give up that line and we're going to the viva voce testimony, but we can't have the advantages of one without the inconveniences of the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, because of the shortness of time, I don't want to take the time to argue that with the Chamber, with all respect. I must respectfully disagree. Whatever can be done by viva voce can be done by 92 ter. Part can be taken in written statement; part can be taken in viva voce. The rule itself says "in whole or part." We can expedite these proceedings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I don't agree at all. Absolutely not. So I am telling you to look at the documents, to go to the documents that you wish to present through the witness, because otherwise this will be a way of getting in by the backdoor new elements with respect to the written statement. So either you're going to adopt this procedure, which has the advantage of gaining time, or you're going to decide to do viva voce, in which case you will ask the witness questions again on the basis of his written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I won't -- because of the time factor I won't belabour it today. I think that that's changed already from the practice that we've adopted in the past few weeks, and I think it's contrary to the jurisprudence of the Tribunal and to the rule. With the greatest respect, there is nothing inconsistent about taking part of the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jurisprudence does not apply to Rule 92 ter. It's a new rule and regulation, so there has been no jurisprudence on that up until the present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am here to control the examination and I am telling you now to ask questions based on the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour, and obviously we will have to re-assess our approach to witnesses and maybe not use 92 ter procedure at all, which unfortunately will slow the procedure down considerably. So I regret this development, but I don't want to take any more time today to deal with it. We will re-assess whether we call any witnesses on 92 ter, then. They may all have to be viva voce.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can then ask, Witness, in light of the Judge's instructions, if you can please turn to Exhibit 1839 in your bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention, sir, to the -- I believe it would be the third page of the Bosnian version or it may be the second page. In the Bosnian version, it is the second page. You can find the words, the paragraph starting "Towards Jablanica there is the village of Lizoperci." If you can find that, please, and tell me when you've found that. You have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. "Towards Jablanica is the village of Lizoperci." I've found that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Looking at those two paragraphs, then, the paragraph starting "Towards Jablanica ..." and the next paragraph which starts with the words "Hudutsko" -- excuse me, "Hudutsko is a purely Croatian village ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "... with 20 conscript-eligible men, conscripts armed with infantry weapons and 60-millimetre mortars. The village of Krevici, towards Konjic municipality, has around 30 conscripts armed with infantry weapons, and it is assumed that they have a gun," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you skipped the line that says: "Toscanica has 80 Muslim houses with about 30 conscription-eligible men armed with infantry weapons and 60-millimetre mortars." My specific question to you, sir, if you can the Judges, is that statement true, or was it true in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. It's not correct at all. There were no mortars, there were no recoilless guns, nothing. The only thing that is true is that there were that number of men, of conscription-eligible men. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was there, as of April 1993, on the Muslim side any military activity in the village of Toscanica, other than the fact, as you say, there were conscription-eligible men located there or who lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No military activities, none at all in the village of Toscanica. In April there were civilians. We organised ourselves as civilians because there was tension everywhere and they'd started taking people off. So you couldn't get the right information. People were afraid, and there were -- was a certain amount of organisation, that, if they should attack, the elderly and infirm would be taken out of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention next, please, to Exhibit P 01955.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And before we get to that, just a small clarification, Your Honour, and I don't mean to disrupt the proceedings, but in that one passage that the Prosecutor pointed to the gentleman, there was a compound, you know, factual basis to that statement. One dealt with -- for instance, it says, "armed with light weapons," and then the other one was to the 82-millimetre mortars. So there are two -- we're talking about two types of weapons. He answered with respect to the mortars, but his -- but if you look at his answer, it would appear that he's also saying no to the light weapons. And the question is: Is that so, that there are no armed men with light weapons? Because later on it would appear that if they're organising themselves, that there might be some light -- so we need some clarification, just step by step. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, fine. Could you make that precision, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in reference -- going back -- I had directed you on to another document, but if you can find your way back to the previous document, if you still have that. In reference to -- you said just a moment ago that as of April 1993 on the Muslim side, there was no military activity in the village of Toscanica. Can you tell us what the status was in terms of any weapons or fire-arms in the village at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I need precision. What day, roughly? Because towards the end, around the 15th of April, there was several of us who had armed ourselves privately and went to Jablanica, to the BH army, which was TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I was among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Prior to that time, prior to approximately the middle of April, what was the status, if you will, of military weapons in the village of Toscanica, prior to the middle of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were four rifles. One was a single-barrel hunting rifle, one barrel; the other had two barrels; and the third was a carbine. And they were -- those two rifles were confiscated later. And the same man had a carbine and another rifle. When he bought the carbine, he'd already had this hunting rifle because he was a hunter. So they're the standard type of rifles that I know. Now, perhaps somebody had some weapons that I didn't know about in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If we can go on, then, please, to the next exhibit where we started before, P 01955.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 501955; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please. Sir, if you can direct your attention to the first page of that document, and in the Bosnian version it may, in fact, only be one page. I'm directing your attention to the first few sentences. It says: "We continue according to plan. We have entered Slatina. ABiH, Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, forces are retreating into Donja Slatina --"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't find that. Can you wait a minute, please. May I take a moment. I apologise, but I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought you had it. Do you have it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, saying: "We continue according to plan. We have entered Slatina. ABiH, Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, forces are retreating into Donja Slatina. Grevici are being surrounded. Lizoperci asked to surrender when they retreated into our Hudutsko. When those from Toscanica heard about this, they asked if the same applied to them. We have blocked Gornji and Donja Duznari [phoen] to prevent defections from Slovici and in order to conduct searches. We targeted artillery support at Slatina." Now, sir, this is a report dated the 18th of April, 1993. Can you assist the Judges by indicating, is that an accurate statement of what was happening in the area of Toscanica on about the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is truth here but not everything is true and correct here. Somebody wrote this arbitrarily. There are elements of the truth there, yes. "Three days ago the forces were on Grevici, Toscanica," and so on, that's true. But this thing with Slatina, I was at Slatina myself when Slatina was attacked. Gornja Slatina was attacked, in fact. It was attacked in the morning without -- it was a surprise attack, and one of our fighters was wounded. His name is Husrep Mujo. He works in the post office but was left without a leg, and he was the only person in the BH army who fell casualty. But Gornja Slatina was free for two days, or rather a day and a night, because our flag, the lily flag, was at the point -- at a point up by Gornja Slatina, because our reconnaissance men told us that Gornja Slatina was empty. And my brother was among them. And at that point, Djulaga Bajramovic, from Lizoperci, swam across the other side of lake Jablanica to Slatina, and he informed the army first that Gornja Slatina was empty, that there were no HVO soldiers in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you to pause there, please. Will you assist me, assist the Judges, in looking at -- in the English translation, and I think if you look, if everyone in the courtroom looks at the B/C/S original you'll see it. The reference is to Toscanica and not to a place called Tosani. Is that correct? The correct name of the village is Toscanica. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, it makes reference to -- it says that the village of Lizoperci asked to surrender. Was that true? And what did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Lizoperci did not surrender, were not supposed to surrender. They held the position at the dam throughout. And when the attack started, the locals left Pudutsko before the locals of Lizoperci because they were promised that nothing would happen, that it was just Toscanica that might be taken and that they would liquidate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, who promised them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That nothing would happen to the locals. The command in Prozor promised them that. I don't know who the main commander was. I know that he was commander of the military police. I think he was Jozo Nestrovic. From 1992, from when the HVO was established, I know that. Now, who the main person was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So that it's clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be permitted. I assume we have now moved back into viva voce mode. This does not seem to be examination about documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's an examination of what happened in Lizoperci which I just asked him which is in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's just -- that's just a device. The witness has never seen this document before. He can't authenticate it. What's happening is that Mr. Scott is defying the Trial Chamber's instruction, using the document as a pretext to conduct an examination-in-chief. If he wishes to switch to viva voce mode, that's one thing. But I think that, as Mr. Ibrisimovic said, I think the Defence is entitled to know what form of evidence we're receiving.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're referring to the documents the same way that we've been using documents with all the witnesses. We direct them to parts that relate to their evidence or to their testimony and ask them if they can give further explanation or confirm the content of the document. This is exactly what we've been doing. And we seem today, for some reason, be making up the rules all over again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. You have the right to ask the question on the basis of what happened in the village, and he said spontaneously that some things in the document were correct and others were not. So you can ask him what was not correct and what was exact in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, if you can explain, sir, when you say the command -- you made reference in your answer a moment ago to the command in Prozor. Which command were you talking about, the command of which armed force or military organisation? What command in Prozor, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at that time when that was going on, I didn't know what command it was. Everybody commanded. One would have to go into details. Our people, together with the Croats, moved towards Kupres, to the line there, because the JNA army was there. Large forces amassed there who were expected -- which were expected to attack Prozor at any time. And the Croats asked us to go together with them to set up a defence. And when we were successful in that, in putting up a defence, an order came one day - now, who the order came from, that should be investigated - one day prior to the attack on Prozor. And it was to the effect that all the Muslims up at the line should be captured. But some of our men down there, from our village in actual fact, noticed. His name was Ilaz Letic, in fact, and Vila Nezir. They noticed this and informed the others. And two platoons managed to pull out through Varvara, Kovacevo Polje, Gornji Toscani, and arrived in the village of Sovici. And from Sovici, they came to Jablanica to inform the others about the situation when Prozor was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back, please, then to -- with all that in mind, to the exhibit you have in front of you now, 1955. Is there anything else that you either -- you say, in that version, a report that you say is correct that you want to confirm or is there anything else that you say is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's not absolutely correct. It can be a Croat, if you like. I don't mind. Half of it's the truth; half of this isn't. Look at Slatina, for example. They claim that they took control of Slatina. Now I'm going to tell you the truth about Slatina. We, that is to say, the BH army, withdrew from Gornja Slatina for one sole reason: It withdrew to the hills above the dam closing off the Jablanica lake towards Doljani, and we did that because there was danger from the village of Hudutsko, because a PAM was set up there --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me stop you, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And a death cellar, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me stop you, sir. What's a PAM?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. What I would like to know first, at the time, during that period, were you a member of the Territorial Defence or were you a member of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time I was a member of the TO of Jablanica, because the 44th Mountain Brigade of Jablanica was being established. It hadn't been actually established, but that's where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Fine. So you were a simple soldier -- or rather, were you a soldier or did you have any special assignments within the unit you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was a reconnaissance man of the 44th Mountain Brigade of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. That means somebody who takes -- you were a dispatch person, messenger, were you, taking telegrams or whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I wasn't. I was -- I went out to search the terrains behind enemy lines. I did reconnaissance work to see whether there were any soldiers, how many, what they were going to do, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you weren't a messenger boy. You were on a reconnaissance -- doing reconnoitring, reconnoitring the enemy positions; right? Yes, you did reconnaissance work, reconnoitring; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Now we see things much more clearly. Proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would have covered that in my questions, Your Honour, if I had been allowed to ask them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And go to the -- you should have gone to the heart of the matter straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to note for the record that none of this has been provided to the Defence in advance, and we're going to have, what, five minutes, ten minutes each to cross-examine? Your Honour, this is absolutely outrageous. If Mr. Scott wishes to do a direct examination of the witness, he should do so and allow us adequate time to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've done exactly what you've asked me to do. I've gone to the statements. I've asked the witness questions about the documents and he's given answers about the documents. And the previous statement talks about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue on the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the answers given, I see that he was in charge of reconnaissance and reconnoitring, which did not appear in the written statement. But as a professional, I ask him proper questions to enlighten us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I understand. As I say, I would have asked the similar questions myself. It is copied in his statement -- it is indicated in his statement, in paragraph 4, that he was trained in reconnaissance, and that's in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can go, please, Witness BU, to Exhibit 1966. If you have -- do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: A report on the 19th of April, 1993. I just want to direct your attention toward the end of the first paragraph. There is this statement, if you can find it, please. You'll see the reference to the word "Toscanica." It says: "In this action our forces encountered very strong resistance, but the Muslim forces were not organised." My question to you, sir: Can you tell the Judges, was there any military resistance in the village of Toscanica on the 19th of April, 1993, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, possibly there was, but on that day when Toscanica was attacked, I wasn't in Toscanica myself, I was in Slatina. That's where I was, Slatina, because there was fighting in Slatina and they attacked Slatina two or three days prior to that. So that's where I was. So when Toscanica was attacked, I heard about it because it's just 2 kilometres from Slatina to Toscanica. Actually, you can hear every shot, let alone grenades exploding and things like that. So, yes, I did hear shooting and I knew what it was all about, what was going on. When I came to Jablanica, there were quite a lot of people from Toscanica, and we asked the commander to go to Toscanica urgently to pull out the civilians. He didn't let us do that, but we nevertheless set out. So we didn't follow his orders, and we left for Toscanica nonetheless. When we arrived in the village of Slatina, we weren't able to cross the bridge at the dam, because you had to pass through Hudutsko to get to Toscanica. So we had to go to Papratsko and take the byroad where we used a boat to go across the lake, and then we saw civilians, women, children fleeing. They were already coming in. And we asked them what the situation was like. They couldn't tell us everything that was going on because there was a lot of crying and people were looking for their nearest and dearest. But we had to get into a boat and go across the lake to the village of Zuglici. This was a mixed village. There were Muslims and Croats living there, and some of them tried, out of revenge, to do something. They said: "Where are the Croats?" or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you to pause. Counsel is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just very brief. I know that Mr. Scott is under pressure with time, and perhaps this is why, you know, he's having some difficulties, but it would be better, I think, or more convenient for all of us and for the record, if he could just take a short narrative so we know exactly where the person was, just in general, during this period. Because, as you see, here he's commenting about a -- he's being asked to comment about an incident when he's not present, that he hears about. I think it's important for background; otherwise, it's going to be impossible for us to cross-examine. And I understand why the Prosecution hasn't done that. But if we could just take some time, just lay the foundation, and I think it might be much better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Witness, you answer in great detail when asked a question. Try to concentrate on the questions put to you. The Prosecutor has the right to ask you questions about the facts, about the defence in your village, which was not well organised. And when he asked you that, you should have told us why the organisation was either good or bad. You answered: "I don't know because I was in Slatina," and then you went on and on about what you did in Slatina. This is very interesting; however, we are obliged here to talk about the essential elements of the contents of the documents in order to make the most of your time. So try to answer precisely when the Prosecutor asks you questions. Mr. Scott, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Again, I have to say, the explanation for what he was doing, the background, is in the statement. It's on -- so, again, if everyone wants to refer to the statement, they can refer to the statement. If we can ask questions about the statement, then we can ask questions about the statement. But there, again, the Chamber has the statement in front of them and I'm not allowed to ask questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So let's go to the next document, Witness. If I can ask you, please, to go to 1976, if you can find that, please. Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the second paragraph on that document it is reported, it says: "Today we carried out operations in Grevici and Toscanica (they were handed over and searched) and Gornja Slatina was captured and occupied." Again, my question to you: Based on your involvement and presence in that area in mid-April 1993, are those statements correct? Or is there any further explanation you can give as to what happened in Toscanica at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I have to tell you that this is not the way we should proceed because anybody can take things out of the context. I would have to provide a detailed answer to every question to avoid that. For example, I am now on one page now and then you move me on to another page. And now, as far as Slatina is concerned, we withdrew from Slatina, as I already told you, and we were already in Donja Slatina. Now you're talking about Toscanica. Toscanica did fall; it was taken. But I wanted to tell you how I arrived in Toscanica and with whom. On that day, we did arrive --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We're going to come to that in a moment. We're going to come to that. If I can just ask you, specifically here what it said in the report is, "handed over." Now, is that correct, that the village of Toscanica was handed over on the 19th of April, 1993, and searched?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. It was not taken. It was destroyed; it was torched. People were killed in it. If you think that this is the notion of surrendering, then I will agree with you. But first I would have to undergo a psychiatric exam before I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you to go toward the latter part of the document, the same document, but if you go toward the latter part of it, you will see this phrase -- this part, the sentence that says: "Tasks were assigned for tomorrow, and Donja Slatina is the focus of operations." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that your assigned position around this time, you've said several times, was, in fact, in Slatina. Is what is stated here consistent with what you know? In fact, around the 19th of April, was the HVO military operation focussed on Slatina? Or did it become focussed in this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but on the 20th -- actually, on the 21st I returned from Toscanica and then I went back to the line. I told you that our line had been set up on the dam at the Jablanica lake, along the hill slope, towards elevation 902, also known as Vita. On the other side of that elevation was Tovarnica, from which you had a view towards Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you, please, then to go on to Exhibit P 09696, which I'm told is currently under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could go into private session, then, Your Honour. I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have that document, 9696 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you've been able to find that document, please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. This is a list of death certificates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is this particular exhibit, 8289, a death certificate for the Ramo Vila, whose body you found in Toscanica on the 20th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did you put a question to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. It is possible, but I don't know. I don't know where this excerpt has been taken from and who took it from wherever it was taken from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Will you look, please, at the -- excuse me. Would you look, please, at the top of the certificate where it has the date. Do you see the 19th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I ask you, please, to look, then, at Exhibit 8477.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is this a death certificate for a man named Ibro Piralic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says so here, but I don't agree with this. This is something that somebody did on their own. And why they did that, I don't know. I'm telling you one thing, and I claim it is correct. And you can show me anything. I suppose that these documents were drafted for some benefits, because they were all buried after their bodies had been exhumed, and it was after the war. I don't know what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, that's in your statement, sir. Did you find -- but you confirm that you found the body of Ibro Piralic in the village of Toscanica on the 20th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that a hundred per cent. I found him and I can tell you exactly where he was and how his body was standing. His body was covered in a long blue coat which was pierced in at least ten places. There were bullet holes, and that's why I concluded that he had been shot with an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to go to Exhibit 8615. Sir, we're not going to have time to go through every photograph, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- you've seen these photographs before. Are these photographs all of the village or surroundings of Toscanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like to see all the photos because one of those photos depicts my house. I saw that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to take you to certain photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please point to your house. Can we see the photo of his house?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Should I take him through the photos, Your Honour? Should we go through them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we should go into private session for that, because if we see the house in open session, somebody might identify the witness based on that. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I fully agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of October, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.10 p.m.,
